Processing_Method: Download Hansen Global Forest Change treecover2000 product clipped to Nigeria. Reclassify: forest = tree cover >= 30% (confirm threshold at implementation — see HAZARD_MODEL_DECISIONS.csv HMD08). Update to 2015 baseline by applying cumulative Hansen loss years 2001–2015 to remove lost forest. Clip to study area. Express as binary: 1=Forest 0=Non-forest.
Key_QC_Rules: Forest definition (30% canopy threshold) must be fixed before G51 computation. Cross-check with G15 (ESA WorldCover class 10 tree cover) — near-agreement expected outside transition zones. Record: total forest area per state in 2015 as baseline statistic. Any cell reclassified as non-forest due to loss before 2015 must be documented in processing log.

Processing_Method: Update G51 by applying Hansen annual loss layers from 2016 to latest available year. Where ESA WorldCover current epoch is available use to cross-validate. Express as binary: 1=Forest 0=Non-forest (or degraded).
Key_QC_Rules: Must be from same source and same threshold as G51 — no mixing of classification methods between baseline and current. Cross-check with G15 class 10 (tree cover) agreement. Timestamp must be documented precisely.

Processing_Method: G53 = G52 − G51. Pixels: +1 = gain (rare in study area); −1 = loss (deforestation); 0 = no change. Compute annual loss rate per state: Annual_Loss_Pct = (Forest_lost_ha / Forest_baseline_ha) × 100. Produce: cumulative loss raster + annual loss time-series CSV per state.
Key_QC_Rules: G52 and G51 must use identical classification parameters. Loss area must be cross-validated against Global Forest Watch statistics for Nigeria (within 10% tolerance for same period). Annual loss time-series must be internally consistent: sum of annual losses must equal cumulative loss. Alert if any state shows annual loss > 5% of baseline (exceptional — verify before publication).

Processing_Method: Quantify deforestation pressure as a function of: (1) proximity of remaining forest to communities (G03) and roads (G16) — closer proximity = higher pressure; (2) recent loss rate from G53 — higher rate = higher pressure; (3) forest patch size from G52 — smaller isolated patches more vulnerable. Normalise and weight (weights per HAZARD_MODEL_DECISIONS.csv HMD08). Aggregate to community-level polygon.
Key_QC_Rules: Proximity decay function must be documented (e.g. exponential decay with 5km half-distance to communities). Patch size analysis requires raster-to-polygon conversion of G52 — document minimum mapping unit. Cross-check: communities adjacent to large intact forest patches should score lower pressure than those adjacent to fragmented forest.
